commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Remove the slow tokenizer mode
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Transformers v5 removed slow tokenizers (huggingface/transformers#40936) and `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` now discards `use_fast`. Since vLLM requires `transformers >= 5.10.4`, `tokenizer_mode="slow"` has been behaving identically to `"hf"`.

This PR:

- Removes `"slow"` from `TokenizerMode`, its handling in `resolve_tokenizer_args` and the benchmark `get_tokenizer`, and its mentions in docs/help text (including the Rust bench CLI)
- Drops `tokenizer_mode="slow"` from the Aria multi-image example
- Removes the remaining no-op tokenizer `use_fast` arguments (Moondream3 processor, tests) and updates a stale comment

The `is_fast` checks are kept because remote-code tokenizers may still be `PythonBackend`. `use_fast` passed to image processors is left alone because it still selects the torchvision backend there, so migrating it to `backend="torchvision"` will be a separate PR.

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for "slow tokenizer" and found no overlapping work.

## Test Plan

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py tests/renderers/test_token_offsets.py -q
```

## Test Result

All 34 tests passed. Pre-commit passes.

No model evals were run because output is unchanged (`"slow"` already resolved to the same fast tokenizer).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to make this change. I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Attention] Bound FlashInfer prefill dequantization scratch
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The FlashInfer TRTLLM prefill fallback for BF16/FP16 queries with FP8 KV allocates temporary dequantized pages for every block-table entry, including unused columns.

Bound the prefill block table using host sequence-length bounds before dequantization. This includes cached prefixes and preserves the contiguous strides required by the dequantization kernel, including for a single prefill row.

For the regression test’s single prefill with 65 KV tokens and 16-token pages, the allocation changes as follows:

| Block-table capacity | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| 64 columns | 65 temporary pages | 6 temporary pages |
| 256 columns | 257 temporary pages | 6 temporary pages |

Counts include the reserved page. These are allocation sizes derived from the implementation and test inputs.

Related open PRs were checked; no duplicate scratch-allocation fix was found. AI assistance was used to implement the change and prepare this description.

## Test Plan

Run the regression test and existing attention/dequantization suites:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_trtllm_attention_integration.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_trtllm_kvfp8_dequant.py -v
```

The new [`test_prefill_dequant_scratch_ignores_unused_capacity`](https://github.com/eopXD/vllm/blob/27197b6ea05497b9929cd186e23094ce2672da3a/tests/v1/attention/test_trtllm_attention_integration.py#L103) checks these cases. Parameters are `(block_size, num_prefills, has_host_lengths, quantize_query)`:

| Reviewer question | Test case |
|---|---|
| Is scratch independent of unused capacity, including a single-row table? | `[16-1-True-False]` |
| Are cached prefixes included and partial pages rounded up? | `[64-2-True-False]` |
| Is the fallback safe without host sequence lengths? | `[16-2-False-False]` |
| Does the FP8-query path retain its original table? | `[16-2-True-True]` |

## Test Result

Passed on the rebased commit:

```bash
  --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD --hook-stage manual

git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

commits.pr_title: [Chore] Use Transformers v5 names and drop redundant processor `use_fast`
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Transformers v5 keeps several v4 names as aliases only. vLLM requires `transformers >= 5.10.4`, so this PR moves to the real names and prevents the old ones from coming back.

### Legacy names

| Legacy | v5 |
| --- | --- |
| `PretrainedConfig` | `PreTrainedConfig` |
| `PreTrainedTokenizer` | `PythonBackend` |
| `PreTrainedTokenizerFast` | `TokenizersBackend` |
| `BaseImageProcessorFast` | `TorchvisionBackend` |
| `XImageProcessorFast` | `XImageProcessor` |
| `transformers.image_processing_utils_fast` | `transformers.image_processing_backends` |
| `transformers.models.<m>.<module>_fast` | `transformers.models.<m>.<module>` |

- Most of the diff is the mechanical `PretrainedConfig` -> `PreTrainedConfig` rename.
- A new `transformers legacy names` rule in `tools/pre_commit/check_forbidden_imports.py` rejects imports of all of the above, including parenthesised multi-line imports and the aliased `tokenization_utils` / `tokenization_utils_fast` modules. The rule has cases in the script's `--test-regex` suite.

### Processor `use_fast`

14 models passed `use_fast=True` to their HF processor, and this PR removes it. In v5 that flag only maps to `backend="torchvision"`, with a deprecation warning. It adds nothing because:

- Without the flag, `AutoImageProcessor` already chooses `torchvision` whenever it is installed. The only exceptions are the Lanczos processors (Chameleon, Flava, Idefics3, SmolVLM) on torchvision < 0.27, and none of these 14 models use them.
- If torchvision isn't installed, forcing the torchvision backend falls back to PIL anyway.
- The flag was passed at the call site, so it overrode `mm_processor_kwargs`. That meant users could not select a backend with `--mm-processor-kwargs '{"backend": "pil"}'`.

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for `PretrainedConfig`/`PreTrainedConfig` and processor `use_fast` and found no overlapping work.

## Test Plan

```
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
python tools/pre_commit/check_forbidden_imports.py --test-regex
# import every changed vllm module
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py::test_processing_correctness[...]  # 18 affected models
pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_jina_ranking_io_processor_unit.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_bailing_moe_v3_vl.py
```

## Test Result

- Pre-commit passes, including mypy and the new rule over the whole repo.
- All changed `vllm` modules import. The exception is `vllm.models.dots3_note.nvidia.vision`, which needs CUDA flash-attention and fails the same way on `main`.
- Processing tests: 31 passed, 3 skipped. The skips were already there: two models require `transformers<=4.57` and one model is not available online.

These tests used Transformers `5.18.0.dev0`. I also checked that every new name exists in v5.10.3.

No model evals were run. Processor outputs are unchanged, and the processing-correctness tests cover every affected model that runs on v5.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to make this change.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Emit MXFP8 from the sparse decode reduce and run wo_a as a grouped FP8 GEMM
commits.pr_body: ## Purpose Follow-up to #57435. That PR moved the inverse RoPE into the sparse-decode reduce epilogue, but the reduce still writes the attention output as bf16 `[T, H, 512]` and `wo_a` then reads it back through a bf16 hipBLASLt einsum (`Cijk_Alik_Bljk_BBS_BH_Bias...`) on a dequantized bf16 copy of the weight. `wo_a` is weight-bandwidth bound at decode, so it pays for twice the bytes the checkpoint actually stores. This PR takes the rest of the chain the way the SM100 path does: the reduce epilogue also emits `wo_a`'s MXFP8 input directly, and `wo_a` runs as a grouped FP8 GEMM on the checkpoint's MXFP8 weight. ``` before: sparse partial -> reduce + inv RoPE -> bf16 [T,H,512] -> bf16 einsum (dequantized W) -> wo_b after: sparse partial -> reduce + inv RoPE + MXFP8 quant/scales -> grouped MXFP8 GEMM -> wo_b ``` ## What changes - **Reduce epilogue (`_sparse_attn_decode_reduce_kernel`, `QUANT_OUT`)**: after the inverse RoPE, the fp32 row is MXFP8-quantized in registers (one E8M0 scale per 32 lanes, the `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` rounding) and stored as e4m3 plus scales. There is no bf16 write, no read-back and no standalone quant launch. - **Grouped MXFP8 `wo_a` GEMM (`rocm_mxfp8_wo_a_bmm`)**: a Triton `tl.dot_scaled` kernel for `[T, G, 4096] x [G, 1024, 4096]` on the CDNA4 MX matrix cores. It reads the e4m3 weight and per-row E8M0 scales exactly as the ROCm MXFP8 linear leaves them after loading, with no scale re-layout and no dequantized copy (the cached bf16 `wo_a` is no longer built: ~33.5 MB/layer at TP2). Tile tiers are keyed on `T * G`, tuned under HIP graphs with a cold weight. It is registered as a custom op, because the tile choice branches on the token count and `_o_proj` runs compiled. - **Prefill rows (`rocm_inverse_rope_mxfp8_rows`)**: sparse prefill still writes bf16, into a workspace slice requested together with the prefill KV gather. One pass then rotates and quantizes it into the same MXFP8 buffer, so a mixed step feeds a single `wo_a` GEMM. - **Layer (`DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention`)**: on gfx950 (`on_gfx950()`), `_alloc_attn_out` returns a `QuantizedActivation` (same contract as the SM100 mega-attention layer), and `_o_proj` runs the FP8 GEMM then `wo_b`. This replaces the bf16 path on gfx950. The bf16 path remains only for archs without MX matrix cores (gfx942), where `wo_a` is BF16-emulated anyway. ## Not a duplicate - **#57081** (open) also targets FP8 `wo_a` on MI355X, but it fuses less. It runs a standalone `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` pass over the bf16 attention output and feeds AITER's `batched_gemm_a8w8_mxscale` after re-laying the 32x32 scales into 128x128. That keeps the bf16 global-memory round trip and adds a launch per layer. It also predates #57435: it targets `vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/`, which no longer exists on main, and is marked as conflicting. This PR fuses more ops into the current path instead. The quant and scale generation live inside the #57435 reduce epilogue, and the GEMM consumes the loaded weight layout directly. The only standalone pass left is for prefill rows, which never had a fused epilogue. - **#57977** chains MXFP8 activations between DeepGEMM kernels on NVIDIA; this PR is the ROCm counterpart for the attention -> `wo_a` hop. - **#57435** is the base this builds on (merged). ## Kernel performance (MI355X, gfx950) The measured unit is the reduce plus `wo_a`. **Before:** reduce + inverse RoPE writes bf16, then the bf16 einsum. **After:** reduce + inverse RoPE + MXFP8 quant, then the grouped FP8 GEMM. XPU Graph delivers significant performance gains for small models and MoE models under low concurrency.

## Purpose

- `InputProcessingContext.get_hf_processor` passes the renderer's tokenizer to `MiniMaxVLProcessor.from_pretrained`, which ignores it. The loader loads another tokenizer and forwards the supplied one to `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained`.
- Transformers deep-copies unknown kwargs into `init_kwargs`, so the renderer's thread-pooled tokenizer is rebuilt. Every cached processor then keeps both the extra tokenizer and a copy of the pool.

- No existing PR or issue covers this. Searched open and closed PRs for MiniMax VL processor tokenizer reuse and supplied-tokenizer reloads.

- Output parity through `MULTIMODAL_REGISTRY.create_processor(..., tokenizer=<renderer-style pooled tokenizer>)` and direct HF processor calls. Compared the old and new loader on text, image, video and image+video prompts, using the MiniMax-M3 tokenizer and processor configs.
- Processor build cost on CPU (transformers 5.17.0), mean of 3 `get_processor(..., processor_cls=MiniMaxVLProcessor)` builds. The tokenizer is prepared like the renderer's: `get_cached_tokenizer` plus `maybe_make_thread_pool` with the default 2 copies.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Frontend] Offload streaming derender detokenization
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57350.

The plain streaming chat and completion derender paths currently `call _detokenize_delta()` synchronously from the FastAPI event-loop thread. Under concurrent streaming workloads, this can serialize derender processing and delay unrelated asynchronous work.

This PR:

- Creates an asynchronous wrapper around `_detokenize_delta()` using the renderer's existing shared executor.
- Awaits that wrapper from both `derender_chat_stream()` and derender_completion_stream().
- `Keeps _detokenize_delta()` synchronous for code already executing within the renderer executor.
- Adds regression coverage verifying that both streaming paths execute detokenization on the configured renderer executor rather than the event-loop thread.
- Streaming derender suite after rebasing onto current `upstream/main`: `60 passed, 1 xfailed` (an upstream test marked as an expected failure)

I searched open PRs by issue number and behavior keywords. #50550 modifies the streaming reasoning/tool-parser path, while this PR targets the plain incremental-detokenization path. The distinction and proposed executor boundary were confirmed in #57350 before implementation.

This changes execution placement only. It does not change tokenization semantics, stream-state handling, output ordering, model execution, or the public API.

**AI disclosure:** This PR includes code developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex during implementation, test design, and review. I reviewed and understood every changed line and ran all tests listed below.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py \
  -q

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py
```

The focused regression test was also run before and after the production change. It exercises both public streaming methods and compares the detokenization thread with the event-loop thread and the configured executor worker.

The performance workload used 20 concurrent streams with 2,048 one-token chunks per stream, for 40,960 derender requests per run. Tokenization probes using a 1,537-token prompt were issued every 250 ms while derender was under load. Each configuration was run three times, and the table reports the median of the per-run measurements.

The benchmark compared `upstream/main` at `6dc34b6334` with this PR at `a1de8533fe`, using `--renderer-num-workers` values of 1 and 4.

## Test Result

- Streaming derender suite: `61 passed, 1 xfailed`
- The expected failure is an existing parser-path case tracked by #55195.
- Ruff formatting and linting: passed.
- Mypy and all other applicable pre-commit hooks: passed.
- Focused regression before the fix: both chat and completion cases failed because detokenization ran on the event-loop thread.
- Focused regression after the fix: both cases passed and ran on the configured renderer executor.

### Concurrent streaming benchmark

| Workers | Version         | Throughput (tok/s) | Derender p50 | Derender p99 | Cadence p50 | Cadence p99 | In-load tokenize p50 | In-load tokenize p99 |
| ------: | --------------- | -----------------: | -----------: | -----------: | ----------: | ----------: | -------------------: | -------------------: |
|       1 | `upstream/main` |            1120.04 |     7.318 ms |    93.818 ms |    7.316 ms |   93.826 ms |            26.974 ms |           104.076 ms |
|       1 | This PR         |            1118.19 |     7.131 ms |    96.195 ms |    7.131 ms |   96.202 ms |            23.564 ms |           102.095 ms |
|       4 | `upstream/main` |            1098.88 |     7.179 ms |   101.206 ms |    7.178 ms |  101.215 ms |            25.042 ms |           107.417 ms |
|       4 | This PR         |            1112.55 |     7.061 ms |   101.228 ms |    7.061 ms |  101.226 ms |            27.383 ms |           131.855 ms |

With one renderer worker, throughput was effectively unchanged (`-0.2%`), median derender latency improved slightly, and in-load tokenization did not regress. With four workers, throughput improved by `1.2%`, median derender latency improved by `1.6%`, and derender and cadence p99 remained effectively unchanged.

The four-worker in-load tokenization p99 median was higher for this PR, although the individual-run ranges overlapped substantially (`93.87–129.97 ms` upstream and `105.89–134.84 ms` for this PR). This may indicate renderer-pool contention or normal tail-latency variance; the benchmark does not distinguish between them. commits.pr_title: [CPU] Gate the AVX10.2 paths on compiler support
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58363.

`cmake/cpu_extension.cmake` requires `gcc/g++ >= 12.3` for the x86 backend, but `csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels` has used AVX10.2 since #49942, and AVX10.2 landed in GCC 15. On anything older the build does not lose a fast path, it fails outright:

```
common.h:537: error: parameter to builtin not valid: avx10.2
gemm_fp8_w8a8.cpp:775: error: attribute 'target' argument 'avx10.2' is unknown
gemm_fp8_w8a8.cpp:777: error: '_mm256_cvtph_hf8' was not declared in this scope
```

Five objects fail, so a source build on any current distro toolchain is broken — Ubuntu 24.04 (gcc 13), Debian 12 (gcc 12), RHEL 9 (gcc 11). `docker/Dockerfile.cpu` is unaffected because it installs `gcc-15` from a PPA, which is why CI does not see this.

This probes for `-mavx10.2` and defines `VLLM_CPU_HAS_AVX10_2` accordingly, guarding the two `target("avx10.2")` helpers and their two call sites. The AVX512 loops directly below each call site already handle the work. On GCC 15+ nothing changes.

The probe mirrors the `-mamx-fp8` handling a few lines above, which gates "on actual flag support rather than compiler version alone" — a version check would also have been wrong here, since AVX10.2 is 15 while AVX10.1 is 14.

## Test Plan

Build `main` plus this patch for CPU on GCC 12.4, and confirm the probe result reaches the guarded translation unit.

## Test Result

`-mavx10.2` rejected by GCC 12.3, 12.4 and 13.4. Configure reports:

```
-- Performing Test COMPILER_SUPPORTS_AVX10_2_FLAG - Failed
-- AVX10.2 disabled: compiler does not support -mavx10.2 (compiler: GNU 12.3.0)
```

In the generated `compile_commands.json`, `gemm_fp8_w8a8.cpp` appears exactly once, under the `_C` target, with no `CPU_CAPABILITY_AVX10_2` but with `CPU_CAPABILITY_AMXBF16` present. So the target-scoped define does reach the guarded unit, and `_C_AVX512`/`_C_AVX2` never compile it — which is why `PRIVATE` on `_C` is sufficient.

Full CPU build on GCC 12.4 completes with no errors: `vllm 0.29.1rc1.dev527+g5fc8113af`, torch 2.13.0+cpu, and `import vllm._C` succeeds. Unpatched `main` fails the five objects above on the same machine.

commits.pr_title: [MRV2] Validate MRV2 entrypoint logits processors
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

MRV2 skipped frontend validation for auto-discovered logits processors, allowing invalid parameters to reach workers. Discover and validate these plugins at admission while preserving pooling's intentional skip.

## Reproducer

A temporary reproducer registers an entry-point-only processor whose `validate_params()` rejects the request, constructs the normal frontend validator, and separately verifies the pooling skip.

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

from vllm.exceptions import VLLMValidationError
from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
from vllm.v1.engine.input_processor import InputProcessor
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor import loader
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor.interface import (
    LogitsProcessor,
)


class RejectingPlugin(LogitsProcessor):
    validation_calls = 0

    @classmethod
    def validate_params(cls, sampling_params):
        cls.validation_calls += 1
        raise ValueError("plugin rejected request")

    def apply(self, logits, ctx):
        return logits


class EntryPoint:
    name = "rejecting"
    value = "reproducer:RejectingPlugin"

    def load(self):
        return RejectingPlugin

    def __str__(self):
        return self.name


def build_validator(runner_type):
    processor = SimpleNamespace(
        model_config=SimpleNamespace(
            logits_processors=None,
            runner_type=runner_type,
        ),
        vllm_config=SimpleNamespace(use_v2_model_runner=True),
    )
    return InputProcessor._build_logits_processors_params_validator(processor)


loader._cached_load_v2_logitsprocs.cache_clear()
with patch.object(loader, "entry_points", return_value=[EntryPoint()]) as discover:
    validator = build_validator("generate")

    try:
        validator(SamplingParams())
    except VLLMValidationError as exc:
        generation_outcome = f"rejected: {exc}"
    else:
        generation_outcome = "accepted invalid request"

    print(f"generation_discovery_calls={discover.call_count}")
    print(
        f"generation_validation_calls="
        f"{RejectingPlugin.validation_calls}"
    )
    print(f"generation_outcome={generation_outcome}")


# Verify that pooling models retain their intentional plugin skip.
loader._cached_load_v2_logitsprocs.cache_clear()
with patch.object(
    loader,
    "entry_points",
    side_effect=AssertionError("pooling unexpectedly loaded plugins"),
) as discover:
    validator = build_validator("pooling")
    validator(SamplingParams())

    print(f"pooling_discovery_calls={discover.call_count}")
    print("pooling_outcome=plugin skipped")
```

### Output on main

```text
generation_discovery_calls=0
generation_validation_calls=0
generation_outcome=accepted invalid request
pooling_discovery_calls=0
pooling_outcome=plugin skipped
```

### Output on this branch

```text
generation_discovery_calls=1
generation_validation_calls=1
generation_outcome=rejected: plugin rejected request
pooling_discovery_calls=0
pooling_outcome=plugin skipped
```

## Test Plan

```text
.venv/bin/python /tmp/repro_mrv2_plugin_validation_full.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_logits_processor_loader.py tests/v1/engine/test_input_processor_trace_replay.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logits_processors.py -q --tb=short
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/logits_processor/loader.py
```

Results:

- deterministic admission reproducer: invalid request accepted on main and rejected on branch
- targeted CPU/H100 suite: 20 passed

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex (GPT-5) assisted with root-cause analysis, the patch, and test execution.

commits.pr_title: [Attention][CPU] Run Zen CPU encoder attention on zentorch SDPA
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

On CPU, encoder / encoder-only attention runs a two-step dance: a reshape-and-cache prologue (`_C::cpu_attn_reshape_and_cache`) stages K/V into a scratch cache, then `_C::cpu_attention_with_kv_cache` reads it straight back on the **same** step — even though an encoder never reuses that cache across steps.

`zentorch::zentorch_sdpa` attends the packed QKV **in place**, so this PR routes encoder / encoder-only attention to it on AMD Zen CPUs when both hold:

- the op is registered (zentorch is built with the SDPA op), **and**
- the model dtype clears zentorch's ISA gate.

Guardrails:

- **Batch shaping** — equal-length batches fold into a single dense call for the whole scheduler batch; ragged batches loop per sequence.

This removes the K/V staging round-trip and runs a faster kernel, concentrating the win on the attention op.

## Changes

Three files, **+254** lines; behavior outside the CPU encoder-attention path is untouched.

- **`vllm/v1/attention/backends/zentorch_sdpa.py`** *(new, +122)* — the encoder-SDPA path, two helpers:
  - `should_use_zentorch_sdpa(attn_type, alibi_slopes, sliding_window, dtype)` — the gate. Returns `True` only for `ENCODER` / `ENCODER_ONLY` layers with **no ALiBi and no sliding window**, when the op is registered (`has_zentorch_op(["zentorch_sdpa"])`) and the dtype clears the ISA gate: `bfloat16` → `torch.cpu._is_avx512_bf16_supported()`, `float32` → `torch.cpu._is_avx512_supported()`; `float16` stays native (no runtime query for AVX512-FP16).
  - `zentorch_encoder_sdpa(query, key, value, output, attn_metadata, scale)` — attends the packed QKV in place (`is_causal=False`, no bias) via `torch.ops.zentorch.zentorch_sdpa.out`, writing straight into `output`. Per-sequence lengths come from `attn_metadata.query_start_loc`; **equal-length** batches reshape to a dense `[B, H, S, D]` and run in **one** call for the whole scheduler batch, **ragged** batches loop per sequence. GQA/MQA needs no expansion — the op derives the KV head count from `key`.
- **`vllm/v1/attention/backends/cpu_attn.py`** *(+32)* — wires the gate into `CPUAttentionBackendImpl`: `self.use_zentorch_sdpa` is computed once in `__init__`, and `forward()` short-circuits encoder attention to `zentorch_encoder_sdpa(...)` and returns **before** the scratch-cache staging + `cpu_attention_with_kv_cache` path.
- **`tests/kernels/attention/test_zen_cpu_encoder_sdpa.py`** *(new, +100)* — numerics vs the `ref_varlen_encoder_attn` reference across uniform + ragged batches, GQA `(8, 2)` and MHA `(4, 4)`, head size `{64, 128}`, `{bfloat16, float32}`; plus a truth table for `should_use_zentorch_sdpa` (ALiBi / sliding-window / decoder / encoder-decoder / `float16` all stay native). Skips on non-Zen CPUs or when the op isn't built.

## Op-level performance

`cpu_attention_with_kv_cache` (baseline) vs `zentorch_sdpa` (this PR). Torch-profiler summary — worker rank 0, `record_shapes=True`; same server and workload, only the attention op differs. Both legs captured an identical **12,312 attention calls across 513 forward passes**.

| Metric | `cpu_attention_with_kv_cache` (baseline) | `zentorch_sdpa` (this PR) | Δ |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| **Attention kernel — self CPU** | **20.527 s** | **12.808 s** | **−37.6% (1.60×)** |
| Attention kernel — avg / call | 1.667 ms | 1.044 ms | −37.4% |
| Attention kernel — calls | 12,312 | 12,312 | — |
| Attention kernel — % of forward | 42.3% | 30.8% | −11.5 pp |
| Attention subgraph — `unified_attention_with_output` | 21.685 s | 14.269 s | −34.2% (1.52×) |
| **Whole forward — self CPU total** | **48.476 s** | **41.542 s** | **−14.3% (1.17×)** |

**Takeaways**

- The kernel itself is **~1.6× faster** (20.53 s → 12.81 s) and the `cpu_attn_reshape_and_cache` staging op (0.86 s) disappears entirely — `zentorch_sdpa` reads packed QKV directly.
- The new path adds ~0.5 s of ATen bookkeeping the staged path avoids: `aten::equal` (~0.44 s, the per-call equal-length batch check) plus small mask/shape ops (`tril`/`triu`/`log`, ~0.1 s). Net attention cost still drops sharply.
- Attention falls from **42.3% → 30.8%** of forward self-CPU time, cutting the whole profiled forward by **14.3%**.

## Test plan

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| **Model** | `RedHatAI/embeddinggemma-300m`, pooling runner (MEAN pooling) |
| **Serve args** | `--dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 2048 --no-enable-prefix-caching` |
| **Workload** | `vllm bench serve --backend openai-embeddings` (random), `--random-input-len 1024 --num-prompts 1024 --max-concurrency 32` |
| **Host** | AMD Zen CPU (`ZenCpuPlatform`), 32 OMP threads pinned to cores 0–31 (`VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=0-31`) |
| **Stack** | vLLM 0.27.0 · torch 2.13.0+cpu · zentorch 2.13.0.0 |

---

commits.pr_body:
Fix UT models/language/generation/test_common.py::test_models[True-False-5-32-microsoft/phi-2] meet OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to C long.

Root cause: PromptEmbedsState.add_request() stores GPU data_ptr() values into a signed int64 numpy array, which only holds up to 2^63-1 CUDA pointers are low and fit; XPU device addresses have the high bit set exceeding int64's max, so numpy raises OverflowError.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CI] Fix the flaky sharded-sampling tests, and the engine teardown need
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

**The two sharded-sampling equivalence tests are flaky.** They were added in
#50465 (commit `d154d90d6c`) to show that batch-sharded sampling is a drop-in
for replicated sampling. On MI355 the non-spec one fails in about 40% of runs:

> AssertionError: 4/16 prompts diverged: beyond near-tie boot-state noise;
> sharded sampling is likely misrouting requests

Sharding is not the cause. Each test compares two engine boots, and with the
engine in its own process prefill starts before the last requests arrive over
IPC, so the boots pick different first batches. That changes the GEMM reduction
order, moves logprobs by up to 0.25 and flips near-ties. The same divergences
appear with sharding disabled on both sides, in prompt logprobs before any
sampling, and on a single GPU where sharding does not exist; they vanish when
the batch holds one request.

**The top-k comparison also misfires.** vLLM appends the sampled token when it
misses the requested top-k, so one side can hold k+1 entries where the other
holds k, and the allowance meant for one near-tie swap is spent on that extra
entry instead.

**Fixing the tests requires fixing engine teardown.** They need the engine in
the caller's process so every request is queued before the first step, but
`InprocClient` never tears its engine core down: unlike `MPClient` it has no
finalizer, and neither `LLM` nor `LLMEngine` calls its `shutdown()`. Its workers
keep their GPU memory for the life of the process, so the second boot fails with
81.5 of 288 GiB free against the 201.6 GiB requested. Seven tests already work
around this by calling `engine_core.shutdown()` by hand.

### What changed

- Both tests run the engine in the caller's process, so the two boots schedule
  the same batches. The divergence tolerances are removed and the comments state
  the measured cause.
- The top-k comparison separates the requested top-k from the sampled token
  before comparing sets.
- `InprocClient` gains the finalizer `MPClient` already uses, with an idempotent
  `shutdown()` so the seven manual calls keep working.

The spec-decode test was never observed failing, since it compares only token
ids over ten tokens. It is changed because the same mechanism applies, its
tolerance rests on an explanation that is not correct, and its own docstring
already asks for exact agreement.

## Test Plan

MI355 (gfx950), two GPUs. Both tests run repeatedly, before and after, to
measure flakiness rather than a single result:

- `pytest -v -s v1/e2e/general/test_sharded_sampling.py`
- `pytest -v -s v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_sharded_sampling.py`

Plus every test that calls `engine_core.shutdown()` by hand, run with and
without the finalizer.

## Test Result

**General test.** Before: ten instrumented runs gave 1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5,
5 divergences out of 16 against a threshold of 3, so about 40% fail. A control
with sharding disabled on both sides gave 2, 2, 4, 5, which is what rules
sharding out. After: five consecutive passes, zero divergences.

**Spec-decode test.** No flakiness observed before, 0 of 120 comparisons; four
passes after. Runtime drops from about 117 s to about 87 s, since the engine now
releases its workers.

**Engine fix.** Without it the second in-process boot fails at 81.5 of 288 GiB
free; with it both boot and memory returns between them.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][V1] Reject encoder-cache hits with mismatched embedding counts
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Addresses the engine-containment part of
[#55546](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55546) and is related to
[#55547](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55547). It does not close
#55546 because frontend multimodal processor-cache (P0) fingerprint/content
validation remains follow-up work.

Keep the encoder embedding count with each V1 multimodal encoder-cache entry and
reject a cache hit when the incoming request expects a different count. Complete
only the mismatched request through the scheduler's existing request-error path,
leaving EngineCore available to later requests.

Client-provided multimodal UUIDs must uniquely identify their data, but accidental
reuse can pair a cached encoder output with a request that expects a different
number of embeddings. The existing
[Multimodal Media UUID Security](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/usage/security.md#multimodal-media-uuid-security)
documentation already assigns UUID uniqueness to the client and documents the
integrity and confidentiality consequences of reuse. This PR leaves that
contract and those risks unchanged while closing the availability gap caused by
different embedding counts.

Related work: [#57833](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57833) makes
`MultiModalReceiverCache` prefer a full payload resent by P0, preventing one
stale processor-payload substitution path. The harmful mismatch in both PRs
requires a client-provided multimodal UUID to be reused for different content;
without a UUID, the cache identity is derived from the media content. #57833
does not validate an encoder-cache entry already retained under that identifier:
if an earlier request completed and left such an entry, scheduling can still
skip encoding the preserved payload and reuse the old encoder output. This PR
checks the embedding count at that admission point; same-count,
different-content reuse remains outside its scope.

If the cached tensor is shorter, the mismatch currently reaches embedding merge,
EngineCore exits, and every subsequent request on that engine fails. If the cached
tensor is longer, slicing can succeed and silently serve embeddings from different
content. Checking counts at cache admission prevents both availability and silent
correctness failures; catching only the merge exception would not cover the latter.
This intentionally changes the longer-cache case from apparent success with
embeddings from different content to an explicit request error.

The old release path also re-derived cache size from the request being released.
With one identifier and different request sizes, that could corrupt freeable
capacity accounting and lead to later allocation assertions.

This PR keeps the existing UUID contract and cache keys. It rejects the request
rather than evicting or re-encoding under a contested identifier. Once admission
is validated, the stale entry cannot make EngineCore unavailable; evicting it on
a client-triggered mismatch would also let that client flush a shared entry that
other requests may still be using.

The request finishes through `FINISHED_ERROR`, which currently represents a
retryable request-level internal error and maps to HTTP 500, even though this
input will fail again until its UUID is corrected. The scheduler has no separate
client-error finish reason, and client-provided grammar compilation failures
already use the same `grammar_compile_error_reqs` drain. This PR reuses that
existing request-scoped containment path; it does not introduce the 500 mapping.

No flag is added because the change converts an engine-fatal condition into a
request-scoped error while preserving behavior for identifiers whose embedding
counts satisfy the existing contract.

For EC connectors, an external load calls `allocate()`, which records the
requesting request's expected count locally. That value is not derived from the
tensor returned by the remote cache, and the arriving tensor's row count is not
compared with it. A first remote hit is therefore outside this validation;
later reuse of the locally recorded entry is checked.

A mismatch schedules zero tokens, but it does not spin: both engine loops still
reach `update_from_output`, which drains and removes the request within one
scheduler step.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k "encoder_cache and embed_count" -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k "mamba_align_encoder_cache_cap_makes_progress or \
eagle3_mm_encoder_cache_with_shift or \
free_encoder_inputs_defers_for_eagle_lookahead or \
encoder_cache_retained_across_preemption_and_resume or \
encoder_cache_recomputed_when_evicted_during_preemption" -v
pre-commit run ruff-check --files \
  vllm/v1/core/encoder_cache_manager.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py
pre-commit run ruff-format --files \
  vllm/v1/core/encoder_cache_manager.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py
git diff --check
```

The GPU comparison runs three sequential SmolVLM requests with
`max_num_seqs=1`: seed a short entry, reuse its identifier for a longer input,
then submit a healthy request under another identifier.

## Test Result

- Five new tests: one encoder-cache-manager lifecycle test and four scheduler
  tests. Three existing manager tests also gain eviction/reset/subclass
  assertions.
- Full encoder-cache-manager file: 21 passed.
- Scheduler tests selected by `encoder_cache and embed_count`: 4 passed.
- Five named adjacent scheduler tests: 5 passed.
- Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check`: passed.

The baseline and fixed GPU arms used the same source baseline, SmolVLM model,
Python environment, and compiled artifacts. The HF processor produced 320 image
tokens for the cached input and 1088 for the later input under the same
identifier.

- Baseline: the mismatch reached V2 worker embedding merge; the mismatched request
  and a later healthy request both reported `EngineDeadError`.
- Final fixed revision: the mismatched request completed with
  `finish_reason="error"`, the healthy request completed, and the process status
  was 0.

The fixed `WARNING` identified `collision-id`, reported that its entry held 320
embeddings while the request expected 1088, and explained that a client-provided
multimodal UUID may have been reused for different content. It contained no
`Attempted to assign`, `EngineDeadError`, or `EngineCore failed` line.

The frontend multimodal processor cache (P0, configured by
`mm_processor_cache_gb`) was disabled to construct cache-lifetime drift
deterministically. A P0 hit reuses the old processed item, while production can
retain an encoder entry after the corresponding P0 entry has been evicted.

Model evals are not applicable. The check only runs while admitting an
identifier-based encoder-cache hit and cannot alter outputs for requests whose
identifier and embedding count satisfy the existing contract.

## Changes

- Store `identifier -> num_encoder_embeds` metadata in `EncoderCacheManager`.
- Preserve it while an unreferenced cache entry remains reusable; remove it on
  eviction and reset.
- Use the stored entry count when updating freeable capacity.
- Compare cached and requested counts before cache-hit admission mutates reference
  state.
- Compare counts when one request repeats an identifier in the same scheduling
  call without double-counting the encoder budget.
- Complete mismatched requests as `FINISHED_ERROR` through the scheduler's existing
  request-error drain.
- Warn with the identifier, cached and requested counts, and likely UUID-reuse
  cause.
- Add coverage for lifecycle accounting, compatible layouts, dangling-reference
  prevention, same-request duplicate identifiers, and scheduler liveness afterward.

The check is entirely in the scheduler and `EncoderCacheManager`, so it applies to
both model runners. The GPU reproduction used the V2 Model Runner.

## Duplicate-work check (2026-09-19)

- `gh issue view 55547 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments`: #55547 is open.
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "55547 in:body"`:
  no open PRs.
- `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "encoder cache multimodal mismatch"`:
  no direct competing implementation was found.

#55549 and #55952 are closed, unmerged prior art. #55583 and #55616 remain open,
but modify processor/rendering and UUID-derivation paths rather than scheduler
encoder-cache admission. #55616 makes reuse more likely by allowing UUIDs to be
derived from URLs, which further motivates validating the cached embedding count.

<details>
<summary>GPU reproduction script</summary>

The short image must run first so its 320-row encoder output is reusable when the
long image requests 1088 rows. The frontend multimodal processor cache is disabled
so each request keeps its own placeholder layout.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validate request-level handling of mismatched encoder-cache lengths."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
import traceback
from typing import Any

from PIL import Image
from transformers import AutoProcessor
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams


PROMPT = "<image>\nDescribe the image briefly."


def make_image(width: int, height: int, color: tuple[int, int, int]) -> Image.Image:
    return Image.new("RGB", (width, height), color=color)


def make_request(image: Image.Image, identifier: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    prefix = f"Image dimensions {image.width} by {image.height}. " * 4
    return {
        "prompt": prefix + PROMPT,
        "multi_modal_data": {"image": image},
        "multi_modal_uuids": {"image": [identifier]},
    }


def count_image_tokens(processor: Any, image: Image.Image) -> int:
    processed = processor(text=make_request(image, "unused")["prompt"], images=[image])
    token_ids = processed["input_ids"]
    if hasattr(token_ids, "tolist"):
        token_ids = token_ids.tolist()
    if token_ids and isinstance(token_ids[0], list):
        token_ids = token_ids[0]
    return token_ids.count(processor.image_token_id)


def generate_once(llm: LLM, image: Image.Image, identifier: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        outputs = llm.generate(
            make_request(image, identifier),
            sampling_params=SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, temperature=0),
        )
        output = outputs[0].outputs[0]
        return {
            "returned": True,
            "finished": outputs[0].finished,
            "finish_reason": output.finish_reason,
        }
    except BaseException as exc:
        traceback.print_exc()
        return {
            "returned": False,
            "exception_type": type(exc).__name__,
            "exception": str(exc)[:500],
        }


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    short_image = make_image(1024, 128, (20, 20, 200))
    long_image = make_image(224, 224, (200, 20, 20))
    healthy_image = make_image(672, 224, (20, 200, 20))

    processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(args.model, local_files_only=True)
    short_tokens = count_image_tokens(processor, short_image)
    long_tokens = count_image_tokens(processor, long_image)

    result: dict[str, Any] = {
        "model": args.model,
        "processor_cache_disabled": True,
        "prefix_cache_enabled": True,
        "token_counts": {"short": short_tokens, "long": long_tokens},
        "token_count_guard": short_tokens < long_tokens,
    }

    if short_tokens >= long_tokens:
        result["guard_error"] = "short image must produce fewer image tokens"
        with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
            json.dump(result, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
            handle.write("\n")
        print("SUMMARY_JSON=" + json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
        return 2

    llm = LLM(
        model=args.model,
        enforce_eager=True,
        enable_prefix_caching=True,
        mm_processor_cache_gb=0,
        max_model_len=2048,
        max_num_seqs=1,
        limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1},
    )

    result["short_seed"] = generate_once(llm, short_image, "collision-id")
    result["long_reuse"] = generate_once(llm, long_image, "collision-id")
    result["healthy_after"] = generate_once(llm, healthy_image, "healthy-id")

    with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
        json.dump(result, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
        handle.write("\n")
    print("SUMMARY_JSON=" + json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))

    return 0 if all(
        step.get("returned", False)
        for step in (
            result["short_seed"],
            result["long_reuse"],
            result["healthy_after"],
        )
    ) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

commits.pr_title: [EPD][Model Loader] Skip language-model checkpoint shards for `--mm-encoder-only`
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

`--mm-encoder-only` already skips building the language model (#30242), but the default loader still iterates every safetensors shard. This PR filters **pure LM shards** out of `hf_weights_files` using the HF weight index before any weights iterator runs: under `--mm-encoder-only`, shards are classified via `_language_model_names` plus the model’s existing `hf_to_vllm_mapper`, pure-LM shards are dropped, and resolve fail-closes (full file list) when an LM module prefix is also an HF ancestor of non-LM mapper entries. Encoder-only EPD cold start therefore avoids reading the full VLM checkpoint on prefix-match families (e.g. Kimi top-level `language_model.` / MiniCPM `llm.`, Qwen nested/flat via the mapper).

**When this helps:** Encoder-only cold start under `--mm-encoder-only` — e.g. EPD Encoder scale-out / restart, or single-Encoder bring-up & testing — by skipping LM-only safetensors I/O when the Encoder never builds the LM.

## Motivation

1. **Finding:** On **[Kimi-K3 pruned75](https://huggingface.co/mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75)**, even the Encoder node under `--mm-encoder-only` still had to walk/load the **full** safetensors shard set — very slow and wasteful for cold start / Encoder restart.
2. **Fix:** Index-based **LM-shard skipping** on the default loader (filter pure LM shards before iterators). Confirmed on that finding: pruned75 **96→2** shards, `Loading weights took` **683.36s → 0.31s**.
3. **Broader check:** Same mechanism validated on **original Kimi-K3**, same-series **Kimi-K2.6**, and **Qwen** (Qwen3 nested + Qwen2.5 flat, classified via `hf_to_vllm_mapper`), including `safetensors` / `instanttensor` / `fastsafetensors` where measured.

They can use the **same** mechanism later with finer non-overlapping HF prefixes or key-level filtering.

Steady GPU memory was already small under Encoder-only; the waste is **startup I/O**, not steady VRAM.

**Environment:** `--mm-encoder-only` · 1xH200 · warm NFS · vLLM **0.29.0** (patched ≡ this PR).

**Gate:** filter only when `mm_encoder_only=True`. Shared-root LM prefixes (e.g. bare `model.` with vision under the same HF root) fail-closed — full file list this PR.

Review asked to avoid a model-specific hard-coded HF nest list and a magic bare-`model.` deny set in the loader.

1. **Prefix source:** `_language_model_names` only → vLLM *module* prefixes (fallback `language_model.`). No per-model override attr.
2. **HF key classification:** map each index key through the model’s existing `hf_to_vllm_mapper`, then test the *vLLM* name against those module prefixes — Qwen nested (`model.language_model.*`) and flat (`model.layers.*` via the catch-all `model.`→`language_model.model.` mapping) need no nest list in `weight_utils`.

- Applies on `DefaultModelLoader` safetensors-file+index path (also `fastsafetensors` / `instanttensor` / `mistral` via the shared file list); other loaders untouched.
- Under `--mm-encoder-only`, derive LM *module* prefixes from `_language_model_names` (fallback `language_model.`) and capture the model’s existing `hf_to_vllm_mapper`.
- `resolve_mm_encoder_only_lm_prefixes()` returns those module prefixes, or `None` (fail-closed → full file list) when a prefix is a shared HF root with non-LM `WeightsMapper` entries (Molmo / Phi-4-MM / Muse).
- `filter_mm_encoder_only_safetensors_files()` reads the index `weight_map`, maps each HF key through the optional mapper, and drops shards whose keys are all LM-module-prefix.
- In `DefaultModelLoader.load_weights`, when multimodal `mm_encoder_only` is set, resolve prefixes + capture mapper, then apply the filter in `_get_weights_iterator` **after** `_prepare_weights` and **before** choosing `safetensors` / `fastsafetensors` / `instanttensor` iterators.
- Missing index / shared-root fail-closed / no key match → unchanged file list (safe).

- Relates to / reopens intent of #30231 (Skip LM weight load).
- Completes **I/O** side of #30242 (module skip already merged).

# [CPU][GDN] Support NIXL DS convolution-state layout

## Summary

Make CPU GDN convolution and recurrent-state handling compatible with both the
NIXL-required DS physical layout and the existing SD layout.

The branch:

- selects DS convolution-state storage automatically when a CPU KV-transfer
  configuration uses NIXL;
- validates and materializes CPU GDN recurrent inputs and state views with
  dense inner strides before entering the native CPU kernels;
- extends native CPU convolution dispatch to accept both SD and DS state
  layouts across prefill, decode, speculative, and multi-token update paths;

## Why

NIXL's Mamba descriptors interpret the convolution state as DS
`[conv_dim_local, conv_rows]`, while the CPU GDN path historically assumed an
SD-compatible view in several native-convolution branches. That mismatch made
the automatically selected NIXL cache layout incompatible with native CPU
convolution and required layout-specific assertions or fallback behavior.

## Duplicate-work Check

Open PR [#49650](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49650),
`[CPU][Spec Decode] Centralize CPU causal-conv dispatch`, is related but not a
duplicate. It centralizes Python-side causal-convolution dispatch for
speculative decoding. This PR instead adds CPU platform layout selection,
NIXL layout validation, recurrent-state staging, and native `conv.cpp` support
for both SD and DS stride layouts.

## Test Plan

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=32 numactl --physcpubind=160-191 -N 5 -m 5 \
```

- Preserve an explicitly configured `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` in `InductorAdaptor` so processes and model configurations can reuse matching compiled kernels.
- Retain model-local Triton defaults when no caller override is supplied, while keeping Inductor graph caches separate for each model configuration.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support `--sse-keep-alive-interval`
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Port the Python frontend's opt-in SSE keep-alive (#51034) to the Rust frontend.

Today, `vllm-rs serve ... --sse-keep-alive-interval 15` is accepted but has no effect. The Rust CLI does not know the flag, so it auto-forwards it to the headless Python engine, where it does nothing. Streaming responses from the Rust frontend therefore stay byte-silent whenever the engine produces no event. That happens during queueing, prefill, long decode gaps, and while a tool parser buffers a whole tool call before emitting it. Reverse proxies and clients with idle read timeouts can close the connection in those windows.

This PR:

- Adds `--sse-keep-alive-interval <seconds>` to the Rust CLI. It has the same semantics as Python: an integer number of seconds, `0` (the default) disables it, and negative values are rejected.
- Stores it as `ApiServerOptions::sse_keep_alive_interval: Option<Duration>`, where `None` means disabled.
- Routes every streaming SSE response through a shared `sse_response(stream, interval)` helper: `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, and `/inference/v1/generate`. When enabled, it uses axum's `KeepAlive`, which sends a comment after each idle interval and resets on every event. The comment bytes are `: keep-alive\n\n`, identical to Python's `with_sse_keep_alive`.

Scope difference from Python: Python wires only chat completions and completions. The Rust frontend applies the option to every SSE response, since the reason for it is the same on every streaming route.

The default path is unchanged: with the flag unset, the response is a plain `Sse` stream, exactly as before.

Duplicate check: no open PR targets the Rust frontend for this. #54424 adds keep-alive to the Python Responses API route, which is a different code path.

## Test Plan

- New unit tests in `rust/src/server/src/utils.rs` run with a paused tokio clock. They drive `sse_response` with an event stream that idles for 20 s between two events, and snapshot the emitted frames together with their timestamps:
  - with an 8 s interval: `data: first` at 0 s, `: keep-alive` at 8 s and 16 s, `data: second` at 20 s
  - with no interval: only the two data frames
- Existing CLI Debug snapshots are updated for the new field.
- Workspace tests, clippy, and rustfmt as in CI.
- Manual CLI check: with `--sse-keep-alive-interval 15`, the flag is no longer forwarded to the managed Python engine command line.

```bash
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --exclude vllm-tool-parser-py --all-features --locked
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
```

`vllm-tool-parser-py` was excluded locally only because it needs libpython on the loader path, and this change does not touch it.

## Test Result

- nextest: all tests passed.
- clippy and rustfmt: clean.
- Not covered: an end-to-end stall through a running server. The route tests use a ZMQ mock engine that needs a multi-thread runtime, where tokio's paused clock is unavailable, so the timing behavior is covered at the helper level. No model evaluation, since the default wire output is unchanged and the option only adds SSE comment lines, which spec-compliant SSE parsers ignore.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change.

## Purpose

DeepSeek V4 Vision checkpoints have `num_nextn_predict_layers=3` and `dspark_block_size=5`. Generic speculative-config logic treats the inherited `n_predict=3` as an MTP divisibility constraint, rejecting valid DSpark `num_speculative_tokens=5`. With an explicit draft model and omitted tokens, it also incorrectly defaults to 3.

## Implementation

Use the existing `use_dspark()` abstraction to keep draft stages independent from parallel draft width. DSpark defaults tokens directly from `block_size`, then `dspark_block_size`, and skips the MTP `n_predict` path. This replaces the V4.1/Gemma4 width-to-`n_predict` workarounds. Non-DSpark defaults and MTP divisibility behavior remain unchanged.

One regression in the existing draft-config suite covers explicit 5 and omitted tokens, asserting that `n_predict` and `num_nextn_predict_layers` stay 3 while `dspark_block_size` stays 5.

## Validation

- On unpatched main `cd10ed6f`, both cases fail: explicit 5 raises `must be divisible by n_predict=3`; omitted tokens resolve to 3.
- `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/config tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py -q --tb=short` in the uv-managed environment: **11 passed**, including after rebasing onto `ec6b14c0`. The changed files are identical to verified commit `598cf964`.
- The same focused current-main suite passed on both ARM64/CUDA Spark nodes: **11 tests per rank**. Normal collection is blocked by missing `tblib`; these runs exclude the parent conftest.
- Nearby `tests/config/test_speculative_draft_max_position_embeddings.py` checks on each rank: **3 passed, 3 failed** because the required Hugging Face repositories were unavailable offline.
- Additional config checks preserve MTP 3/5/6 accept/reject/accept behavior and explicit/default DSpark widths for DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Gemma4, and Qwen3.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/config/speculative.py tests/config/test_speculative_draft_hf_overrides.py`: all applicable hooks passed, including pinned Ruff, typos, mypy, and config validation.

### DGX Spark TP2 evaluation — September 15

A minimal backport onto the qualified Vision runtime `0f1d3dcb` passed 13 config tests and live DeepSeek V4 Vision inference. Both ranks reported `n_predict=3`, `num_nextn_predict_layers=3`, `dspark_block_size=5`, and `DSparkDraftModel` with 5 speculative tokens. Health/model identity, a bounded exact-text canary, and a deterministic red-left/blue-right native-image canary passed. DSpark recorded 43 rounds, 215 draft tokens, and 127 accepted tokens, with acceptance at all five positions.

## Related work

This refactors the existing PR. #55362 fills a missing `n_predict` from width but leaves an existing 3 unchanged; #51338 changes checkpoint-method inference and still retains the generic `n_predict` constraint. Neither supplies this separation for the 3-stage/5-token case.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept custom chat roles for HF templates
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The Python Chat Completions API accepts roles outside the OpenAI set and passes them through to chat templates (`CustomChatCompletionMessageParam`, since #4758). The Rust frontend's HTTP `ChatMessage` is a closed enum tagged by `role`, so the same request fails with HTTP 400 before rendering.

Some public templates depend on this. The `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` chat template maps a leading `root` message to its high-priority system prompt, replacing the default model identity text, while `system` / `developer` go to the lower-priority developer prompt. Under the Rust frontend, callers that override the identity with `root` are rejected.

Changes:

- **HTTP DTO:** add `ChatMessage::Custom { role, content }`. The serde derive now uses `remote = "Self"` and covers only the standard roles; hand-written `Serialize` / `Deserialize` impls dispatch on the role tag. Standard roles go through the derived impl unchanged, and any other string role becomes `Custom`. A `#[serde(untagged)]` fallback variant was rejected: serde falls back to it whenever the tagged variant fails, so a malformed standard message (e.g. a `tool` message without `tool_call_id`) would be silently accepted as a custom role, and field errors would be replaced by the generic untagged-enum error.
- **`vllm-chat`:** add `ChatMessage::Custom`, `ChatRole::Custom(String)`, and `ChatMessage::custom()`. The HF renderer passes the role string to templates unchanged (`TemplateMessage` now borrows its role). Media in custom-role content is collected like other content-bearing roles.
- **Native renderers** (DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 / V4.1, Harmony, Inkling, Kimi K3) reject custom roles with a new `Error::UnsupportedChatRole`, classified as a request validation error (HTTP 400) rather than an internal template error.
- `name` on custom-role messages is dropped, consistent with how the Rust frontend treats `name` on the other roles (Python forwards it to the template).

Duplicate check: searched open PRs for custom / `root` chat roles in the Rust frontend; none found.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change and description.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd rust
cargo nextest run -p vllm-server -p vllm-chat
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all --check
```

New tests:

- `prepare_chat_request_accepts_custom_role_messages`: a `root` message in the request JSON lowers to `ChatMessage::custom("root", ..)`.
- `chat_http_message_keeps_standard_role_errors`: a `tool` message without `tool_call_id` still fails with `missing field \`tool_call_id\``.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Recognize new frontend-owned serve args as unsupported or no-op
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Several frontend-owned arguments were added to Python `vllm serve` after the Rust CLI's reference revision (`bc2c0c86ef`). The Rust CLI does not declare them, so they are silently ignored on both launch paths:

- `vllm-rs serve` auto-forwards unknown flags to the headless Python engine, which accepts them but never reads them, because they are consumed on the API-server side.
- In `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve`, they reach the Rust frontend in `--args-json`, where serde drops unknown keys.

For example, `--max-num-queued-reqs 64` looks accepted, but no admission control happens.

This PR declares them in `UnsupportedArgs` with the existing markers, so that setting one either fails with the usual "not implemented in Rust frontend yet" error or warns as a no-op. None of them is plumbed.

`Unsupported`:

- `--fingerprint-mode`, `--fingerprint-value` (`system_fingerprint` on responses)
- `--max-num-queued-reqs`, `--max-num-queued-tokens` (API-server admission control, HTTP 503)
- `--enable-per-request-metrics`
- `--mm-hasher-algorithm`, `--mm-tensor-ipc`, `--mm-processor-device`, `--mm-ipc-gpu-memory-gb`
- `--enable-fault-tolerance`

`Noop` (Python-internal knobs with no Rust counterpart):

- `--renderer-num-workers` (Python renderer thread pool)
- `--enable-flash-late-interaction` (GPU MaxSim for pooling scores in the API-server process)

The default path is unaffected. `RustFrontendProcessManager` sends only non-default args (`jsonify_non_default_args` compares against fresh parser defaults), so a plain `vllm serve`, or one that passes default values explicitly, sends none of these keys.

Intentionally left undeclared:

- `--sse-keep-alive-interval`, which is implemented in #58306.
- Cohere-specific `--cohere-format` and `--cohere-is-reasoning-model`.
- DP-supervisor args (`-dpm`, `--data-parallel-supervisor-port`, `--dp-supervisor-probe-*`): they are consumed by the Python launcher, and the Rust frontend should stay unaware of them.
- Shared engine args whose engine-side effect still works with the Rust frontend, e.g. `--mm-device-do-normalize`, `--reasoning-config`, `--aux-output-config`, and `--return-sampling-mask`.

## Test Plan

```bash
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-managed-engine
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-managed-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CPU][MoE] Fix out-of-bounds write and segfault when router weights are fp32
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

On the CPU backend, serving an MoE model whose router weights are fp32 corrupts the heap on every router GEMM, and the process dies with a SIGSEGV or a glibc abort. Hunyuan-V3 crashes during warmup, before it answers a single request. MiniMax-M2 and Nemotron-H build their routers the same way. Models that set only `out_dtype=torch.float32` keep bf16 weights and are unaffected.

How it happens:

1. `GateLinear` stores MoE router weights in fp32, and decides whether to upcast the bf16 activation by comparing `x.dtype` to `self.weight.dtype`.
2. `dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm` builds the GEMM primitive from the real fp32 weight, then with `remove_weight=True` frees the weight by rebinding it to placeholder `torch.empty(0)` without explicitly setting `dtype`. The original weight dtype is forgotten in the process and replaced by the default torch dtype, let's say bf16
3. In forward with a bf16 input, `GateLinear` skips the upcast, and passes a bf16 `x` to `ops.onednn_mm`, which sizes the output buffer from `x.dtype` while the primitive it calls still writes fp32, leading to invalid memory access.

This PR sets `dtype` explicitly at the three removal sites, using the `dtype` already captured above them, so the placeholder keeps the weight's dtype and step 1 compares against the real one.

Related: #27465 fixed a different route to the same corruption, and named the assumption this one breaks — *"I supposed all handler should use same dtype in a inference instance (process)"*.

## Test Plan

New parametrized case in the existing dispatch test, over the three weight dtypes:

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/test_cpu_unquantized_gemm_dispatch.py -v
pre-commit run -a
```

It forces the zentorch branch through the file's existing `_mock_zentorch_linear_unary` fixture, so it is deterministic on any host and needs no oneDNN dtype support.

Manual check of the real crash, before the fix:

```python
import torch
from vllm.model_executor.layers.utils import cpu_unquantized_gemm, dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm
from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_default_torch_dtype

layer = torch.nn.Linear(4096, 192, bias=False, dtype=torch.float32)  # an fp32 MoE router
with set_default_torch_dtype(torch.bfloat16):  # what base_loader.py does while loading a model
    dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm(layer, remove_weight=True)
print("weight dtype:", layer.weight.dtype, flush=True)  # bfloat16, was float32

x = torch.randn(1, 4096, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
cpu_unquantized_gemm(layer, x, layer.weight, None)  # writes 768 bytes into a 384-byte buffer
```

## Test Result

Before, the three new cases fail and the placeholder's dtype is the ambient default:

```
test_dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm_remove_weight_keeps_dtype[weight_dtype0] FAILED
test_dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm_remove_weight_keeps_dtype[weight_dtype1] FAILED
test_dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm_remove_weight_keeps_dtype[weight_dtype2] FAILED
E       assert torch.float32 is torch.bfloat16
E       assert torch.float32 is torch.float16
E       assert torch.bfloat16 is torch.float32
3 failed, 3 passed
```

After: `6 passed`. The manual script above runs to completion instead of aborting, and a 4-layer Hunyuan-V3 serve that previously died during warmup now completes a request.

AI assistance: root cause, patch and test were produced with Claude Code; I reviewed and ran everything.

[Bugfix][KV Offload] Retain offload event metadata through batch translation
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`OffloadingEventsTracker` caches a `BlockStored` payload per offload key and drops it when the key's last residency goes away. The drop happened inline in `_take_removed_event`, so within a single `take_events` batch a removal could delete the payload that a *later* event in that same batch still needed — a primary removal preceding a queued secondary (KVCR) store. That store then fell back to the placeholder payload, publishing an event with no block hashes and no token ids.

Fix: collect the removed keys during the batch and drop their payloads once, after every event in the batch has had a chance to register its residencies.

Scope: this does not address a store that only completes in a later batch; that needs the in-flight store set and is left for a follow-up.

Not a duplicate of #52103, which touches the same files to add request provenance to stored events.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py
```

`test_primary_removal_preserves_metadata_for_same_batch_kvcr_store` is added to the existing suite, parametrized over the secondary removal landing in the same batch or the next one. It asserts the store keeps its full payload, and that the payload is still dropped once no residency remains.

## Test Result

```
25 passed, 14 warnings in 18.96s
```

Both parametrizations fail with the fix reverted and pass with it applied. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes (ruff, ruff format, mypy).

No model evaluation: this changes only the KV-event payload published to external consumers, not the offload data path or any generated output.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Give turboquant boundary layers a layout-compatible backend
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The `(MI300) LM Eval TurboQuant KV Cache` group, added by [#50519](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50519), fails all four of its tests in [AMD CI build 12548](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12548/list?sid=01a0609c-72b4-4312-b09a-ec5852db1fc7&tab=output). Each server exits during startup with:

```
ValueError: No KV cache layout satisfies every supported set: [['LHBNC', 'LBHNC'], ['LBNHC']].
```

A `turboquant_*` KV cache never covers the whole model. `TurboQuantConfig.get_boundary_skip_layers` keeps the first and last two attention layers of a dense model at the native dtype, so those layers select an attention backend of their own while every other layer selects `TURBOQUANT`. On ROCm they land on `ROCM_ATTN`, first in the platform's priority list, which reads `LHBNC` or `LBHNC` and keeps the K and V groups in separate planes. `TURBOQUANT` reads only `LBNHC`, because it packs K and V into one slot per token and head. One layout has to serve the whole worker, so the intersection is empty and `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` raises.

This treats an empty intersection as a reason the backend is invalid for the layer. The boundary layers then get `TRITON_ATTN`, which is stride-aware and declares no layout preference, and the run resolves to `LBNHC`. The same filter applies to an explicit `--attention-backend`, a path that already tolerates a mismatch on a `turboquant_*` run because no single backend can serve every layer. Runs whose KV cache dtype is not `turboquant_*` are unaffected.

## Test Plan

On one MI300X (gfx942), the failing group itself:

```bash
pytest -s -v evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py \
    --config-list-file=configs/models-turboquant.txt
```

and the ROCm selector unit tests:

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py
```

## Test Result

The group is green, 4 passed in 10m35s over all 1319 questions per config.

commits.pr_title: [Test][Determinism] Cover chunked prefill in the batch-invariance suite
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Batch invariance is what stops the same request coming back with different text
depending on how busy the server was. `tests/v1/determinism/` guards that — but
not for chunked prefill, which is what a loaded server does constantly: a long
prompt is split across several scheduler steps, and the later chunks attend over
KV computed in the earlier ones.

The suite says so itself, in a TODO left by #32561:

```python
# TODO: Update prompts to have ragged lengths in order to test chunked prefill
#       The above tests are not currently long enough to exercise chunking.
```

It is accurate. Every prompt in
`test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_bs1_vs_bsN` is short — 356 tokens for
the whole 32-prompt batch against a default budget of 2048 — so a prefill is
never split, and nothing checks that a user gets identical output whether or not
the scheduler chopped their prompt up.

## What this adds

`test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_ragged_chunked_prefill`: a ragged batch
of short, medium and long prompts with the token budget set below the longest
prompt, asserting bitwise-identical logprobs and identical sampled tokens
between bs=1 and bs=N.

I checked against the scheduler that prefills really are split, and that bs=1
and bs=N split the *same* prompt differently — different chunk boundaries, and
sometimes a different number of chunks. That difference is the point: the output
has to stay put regardless.

The budget is derived from the tokenized prompts rather than hardcoded, so the
test cannot quietly stop chunking if `VLLM_TEST_MODEL` changes the tokenizer.
`LLM_with_max_seqs` gains an optional `max_num_batched_tokens` (default `None`).
No non-test code is touched.

## Test Plan

1x RTX 3060 (12 GiB, sm_86), on the default model `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B`:

```bash
VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.5 pytest \
  tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py -q -k ragged_chunked_prefill
# 3 passed in 115.52s   (FLASH_ATTN, TRITON_ATTN, FLEX_ATTENTION)
```

Re-run with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0` it fails on every prompt on every backend
(42/42), so it can actually catch a regression. The needle test — the only other
caller of the helper — still passes (6 passed, at reduced settings to fit
12 GiB). `pre-commit run --files ...` is clean.

**SM90 confirmed** — @yuvalluria ran the three parametrisations on an H100 NVL
(Torch 2.13.0+cu130, vLLM 0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b): FLASH_ATTN,
FLEX_ATTENTION and TRITON_ATTN all pass, 3 passed in 208.27s. That covers the
path I could not reach on sm_86, where the Triton matmul overrides and cuBLAS
workspace pinning differ.

The A100/H100/B200 Batch Invariance jobs in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`
run this file with no `-k` filter and list `tests/v1/determinism/` in
`source_file_dependencies`, so CI will exercise it on all three.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DSA] Bound DeepSelect sentinel columns in the sparse top-k remap
commits.pr_body:
## Problem and fix

DSV4.1 startup can hit a CUDA illegal memory access in `_sparse_topk_remap_kernel`. Dummy runs feed NaN indexer logits by design (`deep_select_topk` disables its NaN trap for this reason). For a row with NaN inside its valid prefix and `end > topk`, DeepSelect writes an internal sentinel (`0x3f3f3f3f`) to slot 0 of the output row and returns without writing the other slots, which keep whatever the `col_indices` scratch held (the previous call's columns, always in `[0, width)` or `-1`). The remap only rejected negative columns, so slot 0 indexed `sparse_indices[row, 0x3f3f3f3f // SBK]`, about 500 MiB past the row. Whether that faults depends on what happens to be mapped there: it crashes on some layouts (observed on TP4) and silently writes garbage positions on others.

Treat columns outside `[0, width)` as invalid, like `-1`. For a NaN row this makes slot 0 `-1`; the other slots remap stale in-bounds columns, which is harmless for the dummy runs that produce NaN logits. Finite logits are unaffected, since DeepSelect only returns columns below `end <= width`.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  -k "sparse_topk_remap or candidate_blocks_to_sparse or sparse_mqa_logits" -q -rs

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/sparse_mqa_logits.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py
```

- **8 passed**, 7 skipped (need a standalone `deep_gemm`) on GB200. The new test fails on main (slot 0 of NaN rows remaps to garbage) and passes with this change; it zeroes the scratch like the production `col_indices_buffer` so it does not depend on allocator contents.
- Single-GPU repro at production shape (width 16384, topk 512, SBK 8, 128 NaN rows, `expandable_segments`): main raises an illegal memory access; with this change every sentinel slot is `-1`.
- Pre-commit passed.
- No model eval: outputs for finite logits are unchanged.

## Related work and AI assistance

Open-PR search found no equivalent fix. #49897 routes SM12x prefill top-k around a different NaN-broken kernel path and does not touch this remap.

On CUDA these Triton sampler warmups recompile on most engine starts (about 110s each, against `finished in 0.00s` before), so NVIDIA CI jobs slowed down a lot and many now time out.

Median passing runtime per step, ~26 `main` builds before vs ~26 after `96e203b08e`:

27 tests in `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py` fail in the `(MI355) Miscellaneous Kernels` job added by #50519, all with the fused RMSNorm enabled:

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Pick a KV block size supported by every attention backend
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #48286.

`Platform.update_block_size_for_backend()` picks the KV cache block size from the **first** non-SSM attention backend only. Models that mix attention backends with disjoint block-size support break: GLM-DSA / DeepSeek-V3.2-style models pair a sparse-MLA main backend (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, supports `[32, 64]`, prefers 32) with `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` (supports only `[64]`). The auto-selected 32 then fails much later in `select_common_block_size()` with the opaque

```
ValueError: No common block size for 32.
```

and the only workaround is a manual `--block-size 64` (undocumented, as #48286 notes).

This PR was split in two to keep the diff reviewable. It now carries backend collection and block-size selection only (+131/-21). Aligning phases 2 and 3 to the full backend list follows in a separate PR once this one merges.

## Changes

- `Platform._find_non_ssm_backend()` becomes `_find_non_ssm_backends()` and returns every distinct non-SSM backend in layer order rather than the first. Both call sites are updated (`interface.py`, `cpu.py`); no caller of the old name remains.
- New `Platform._preferred_block_size_for_backends()` returns the smallest block size every backend accepts:
  - a single backend keeps today's behaviour via `get_preferred_block_size()`;
  - if every backend accepts the default, the default wins;
  - otherwise candidates are the least common multiples formed by taking one supported size per backend, tried in ascending order, and **each candidate is confirmed against every backend** via `supports_block_size()`;
  - if nothing is common it raises `ValueError` naming each backend and its supported sizes.
- Candidates are validated rather than inferred. A backend may override `supports_block_size()` to accept exact sizes only, as CPU_MLA does by accepting 16 but no multiple of it, so "a multiple of a supported size" is not a safe assumption. This is the correctness point @yewentao256 raised in review.
- Phase 1 of `update_block_size_for_backend()` uses the new selection, and the log line now names all participating backends.
- Phases 2 and 3 are unchanged here and still take the first backend, exactly as before this PR.

## Test Plan

New unit tests in `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py`, built on a `_mock_backend` helper that can emulate an exact-size backend:

- `test_preferred_block_size_satisfies_every_backend`, parametrized:
  - a lone `MultipleOf(8)` backend keeps the default 16;
  - `[32, 64]` plus `[64]` gives 64, the #48286 shape;
  - `[32, 64]` alone still gives 32;
  - `[32]` plus `[48]` gives 96.
- `test_preferred_block_size_searches_past_an_exact_size_backend`: an exact-size backend accepting `[16, 96]` beside `MultipleOf(32)` gives 96, where a greedy lcm(16, 32) = 32 would be wrongly accepted.
- `test_preferred_block_size_rejects_backends_with_no_common_size`: an exact-size `[16]` backend beside `MultipleOf(64)` raises `ValueError`.

## Test Result

- The new unit tests and the existing `select_common_block_size` tests pass.
- End-to-end on GLM-5.2 NVFP4 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), PP=2 / TP=8 / `--enable-expert-parallel`, Ray executor, 2 nodes x 8x B200. This run was performed on the pre-split branch, whose phase 1 selection is what this PR retains. Previously it crashed at KV-cache init without `--block-size 64`; with the change it boots with no block-size flag, logging

```
Setting kv cache block size to 64 for DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER/FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE backend(s).
```

and serves correct output (temperature-0 smoke).
